old.name: Casa-Museu Salvador Dalí — Portlligat
old.hook: The labyrinthine fisherman's-shack house where Dalí lived 1930–1982, entered in groups of a handful every ten minutes.
old.text: The labyrinthine fisherman's-shack house where Dalí lived 1930–1982, entered in groups of a handful every ten minutes. Dalí bought a one-room hut from the fisherman Lídia Noguer in 1930 and spent fifty years annexing the cottages around it into a warren of seven levels that climb the Portlligat hillside — the egg-topped tower, the oval Gala room, the studio with its sunken easel pit, and the lip-shaped sofa. The Fundació Gala-Salvador Dalí runs it as timed-entry only: groups enter every 10 minutes, self-guided with staff stationed inside, and advance booking is always required. The olive grove and pool with the Michelin-man Pirelli figure are visible from the cheaper grounds ticket. It is not wheelchair-accessible — the house is all narrow stairs and split levels. Closed 7 January to 11 February each year. Book timed tickets in advance at salvador-dali.org; arrive 30 min before your slot or the ticket is voided (no refunds). T. +34 972 677 500 / reserves@fundaciodali.org · €15 online / €17 at the door full; €12 / €14 reduced (students, over-65s); olive-grove-only €8 / €6; free ages 0–8. Verified on the Fundació site, 2025 rates. · Jun 15–Sep 13 daily 09:30–20:00; most of the rest of the year Tue–Sun 10:30–18:00; closed Jan 7–Feb 11. · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Museu de Cadaqués — the town's own gallery
old.hook: A small museum in the centre running rotating shows on the artists who painted this bay — Dalí among them.
old.text: A small museum in the centre running rotating shows on the artists who painted this bay — Dalí among them. Unlike the house at Portlligat, the Museu de Cadaqués sits in the heart of the old town and mounts temporary exhibitions tied to the village: painters and themes connected to Cadaqués and its light, with recurring shows on Salvador Dalí and on the Pitxot family, the local clan of artists and musicians who first drew Dalí into the colony. Compact, climate-controlled, a good hour out of the tramuntana. Hours below are from a tourism aggregator — verify against the museum before relying on them. (Check current opening hours before going.) Walk-in; centrally located in the old town. Check current exhibition before going. · Modest admission (confirm on site). · Closed Tuesdays; roughly Mon and Wed–Sat 10:30–17:30, Sun 10:30–14:00 (verify seasonally). · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: The artist colony — why everyone came
old.hook: Picasso painted here in 1910; by the 1920s–30s Cadaqués pulled in Duchamp, Lorca, Buñuel, Magritte and Éluard.
old.text: Picasso painted here in 1910; by the 1920s–30s Cadaqués pulled in Duchamp, Lorca, Buñuel, Magritte and Éluard. Cadaqués was a hard-to-reach fishing village — no easy road until the 20th century — which is exactly why artists treated it as a private retreat. Picasso worked here in the summer of 1910. In the 1920s and '30s Dalí's family summer house became a hub: in the pivotal summer of 1929 Dalí hosted Luis Buñuel, René Magritte and Georgette, and the poet Paul Éluard with his wife Gala — who left with Dalí and never went back. Marcel Duchamp summered here for years and played chess on the front; Federico García Lorca, the writer Josep Pla, and later Mick Jagger and Gabriel García Márquez all passed through. Dalí called it 'el lugar más bonito del mundo.' A walking theme, not a ticket — trace it through the waterfront, L'Hostal, and the Museu de Cadaqués. · Free (self-guided walk). · Anytime. · Open in Google Maps →

old_also.name: The village's musical clan — the Pitxots
old_also.hook: The family of musicians and painters who first pulled Dalí into Cadaqués culture.
old_also.text: The family of musicians and painters who first pulled Dalí into Cadaqués culture. Cadaqués's deepest musical thread is local: the Pitxot (Pichot) family — among them the painter Ramon Pitxot, who first showed the young Dalí modern painting, and the operatic and instrumental musicians of the same clan — were the artistic dynasty that made the village a salon long before the festival. Their legacy surfaces in the rotating shows at the Museu de Cadaqués, which has mounted Dalí-and-Pitxot exhibitions tying the family's music and art to the bay.

old.name: Església de Santa Maria — the fishermen's altarpiece
old.hook: A 23-metre baroque retaule of gilded wood, paid for by the fishermen's brotherhood, carved 1723–1729 and not fully gilded until 1788.
old.text: A 23-metre baroque retaule of gilded wood, paid for by the fishermen's brotherhood, carved 1723–1729 and not fully gilded until 1788. The whitewashed church crowns the old town; climb the stepped, schist-cobbled lanes (the local stone is slate/schist, set on edge) to reach it. Inside, the main altarpiece by the sculptors Pau Costa and Joan Torras rises 23 metres by 12 — a gilded baroque façade in five tiers, from a predella of Passion scenes up through the Marian central body to the attic, with the four Evangelists and the Coronation of the Virgin. The carving was done 1723–1729; the gold leaf was only finished in 1788, financed across decades by the town's fishermen, whose brotherhood paid for the work. Summer church concerts of the Festival de Música use the nave for its acoustics. Visiting hours are not officially published online — verify locally. Free entry outside service hours; the church doubles as a festival concert venue in summer (ticketed for those events). · Free to visit; festival concerts ticketed separately. · Generally open daytime; verify locally — hours not officially published online. · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Cementiri de Cadaqués — graves above the water
old.hook: A small hillside cemetery behind the church, its tombs looking straight out to the Mediterranean.
old.text: A small hillside cemetery behind the church, its tombs looking straight out to the Mediterranean. Reached by going around the back of Santa Maria, the village cemetery is a quiet terrace of whitewashed niches and family tombs stacked against the slope, every row facing the sea. It is modest — a handful of documented memorials — but the position, between the baroque church above and Dalí's bay below, makes it one of the calmer high points to take in the whole sweep of roofs, water and the Cucurucú rock. Free; walk up past Santa Maria and around the church. · Free. · Daytime open access. · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Far de Cap de Creus — the lighthouse at Iberia's edge
old.hook: The easternmost point of mainland Spain, lit since 29 July 1853, on a wind-scoured headland of folded schist.
old.text: The easternmost point of mainland Spain, lit since 29 July 1853, on a wind-scoured headland of folded schist. Drive or walk the 8 km of switchbacks east out of Cadaqués to the cape, where the lighthouse — operational since 29 July 1853 — stands above coves like Cala Fredosa and Cala Jugadora. This is the tramuntana's anvil: the north wind has twisted the schist and slate into the contorted shapes Dalí mined for his melted forms. The headland sits inside the Parc Natural de Cap de Creus, Catalonia's first marine-and-land natural park. A restaurant occupies the old keeper's building beside the tower; the views run from the Pyrenees to the open Mediterranean. Headland/exterior hours and any interior-museum fee are seasonal and not officially published — confirm before going. Free to reach the headland and lighthouse exterior; restaurant beside the tower for food/drink. Park at the cape (fills fast in summer). · Free (headland/exterior). · Headland open access; lighthouse interior museum opens seasonally (summer). · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Espai Cap de Creus — reading the rock
old.hook: The natural-park interpretation centre at the cape that decodes the geology Dalí turned into Surrealism.
old.text: The natural-park interpretation centre at the cape that decodes the geology Dalí turned into Surrealism. Set in the converted buildings around the lighthouse, Espai Cap de Creus is the scientific visitor centre for the Parc Natural — it lays out the geological evolution of the peninsula (the folded schists, pegmatite veins and wind-eroded forms) alongside the flora and fauna of the headland. It is the place to understand why this coast looks the way it does before you walk the GR-11 trails out to the cape's tip. Opening is seasonal (mainly summer); confirm on the Parc Natural / Empordà Turisme listing before going. Visit alongside the lighthouse at the cape; opening is seasonal, check the Parc Natural / Empordà Turisme listing before going. · Check on site; small/free interpretation centre. · Seasonal (mainly summer); confirm before visiting. · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Festival Internacional de Música de Cadaqués
old.hook: Catalonia's second-oldest summer festival, born in the church in August 1970.
old.text: Catalonia's second-oldest summer festival, born in the church in August 1970. Founded in 1970 — the second-oldest festival on the Costa Brava after Sant Feliu's Porta Ferrada — it runs across roughly April to December (10 concerts in the 52nd edition, 2025) split between the Església de Santa Maria and the Espai Art i Joia. The 2025 line-up ranged from the Orquestra Barroca Catalana and guitarist Carles Trepat to a trumpet-and-saxophone night with Mireia Farrés and Llibert Fortuny, closing 27 December with mezzo-soprano Titon Frauca and organist Pau Riuró. In 1988 the festival spun off its own Orquestra de Cadaqués.

old_also.name: Church concerts in Santa Maria
old_also.hook: Baroque and chamber programmes under the 23-metre gilded altarpiece.
old_also.text: Baroque and chamber programmes under the 23-metre gilded altarpiece. The festival uses the nave of Santa Maria for its acoustics: 2025 dates included the Cor i Orquestra de l'Orfeó Gracienc (13 April), the Orquestra Barroca Catalana (24 May), Carles Trepat solo guitar (5 July) and the Quartet Prysma (23 August), most at 19:00. Hearing a Bach partita or a baroque ensemble beneath the Pau Costa retaule is the single most site-specific musical experience in the village.

old.name: Havaneres & cremat
old.hook: Cuban-rooted sea-shanties sung over flamed rum-coffee.
old.text: Cuban-rooted sea-shanties sung over flamed rum-coffee. The Costa Brava's signature ritual: havaneres — choral songs in the rhythm of the Cuban contradansa, carried back by 19th-century Catalan sailors trading with Cuba — sung while cremat (rum, sugar, cinnamon, lemon peel and coffee, flambéed in a cauldron) burns blue in the dark. The genre's epicentre is the Cantada d'Havaneres at nearby Calella de Palafrugell on the first Saturday of July, where choirs like Port Bo perform; Cadaqués and the other Empordà ports keep the tradition in summer terrace sing-alongs.

old.name: Cap Roig Festival (nearby)
old.hook: Big-name open-air pop in a clifftop botanical garden, ~79 km down the coast.
old.text: Big-name open-air pop in a clifftop botanical garden, ~79 km down the coast. Held in the gardens of Cap Roig at Calella de Palafrugell (about 79 km / just over an hour by road from Cadaqués), the festival ran 12 July–18 August in 2025 with headliners including Tom Jones, James Blunt, Franz Ferdinand, Simple Minds and Sopa de Cabra. It is the region's heavyweight summer concert series — the place to go for arena acts when Cadaqués itself stays small and acoustic.
